rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala is agreed to be Qur'an in 27:30, but scholars dispute its status at the start of al-Fatiha and each sura; al-Shafi'i's group affirms it and Abu Hanifa's group does not.
rows.anchor: سورة النمل , وإنما اختلفوا في

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: He and others treat bi-sm as an extra connective, so the intended wording is Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate.
rows.anchor: فذهب أبو عبيدة وطائفة إلى

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: His verse uses ism as an extra word, evidence for treating bi-sm as connective rather than essential.
rows.anchor: ثم اسم السلام عليكما … ومن يبك

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: On the extra-word reading, ism magnifies and honors God's mention, distinguishing it from mention of creatures.
rows.anchor: المخلوقين , وهذا قول قطرب

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: On the extra-word reading, ism shifts the phrase away from an oath and toward seeking blessing.
rows.anchor: قصد التبرك , وهذا قول الأخفش

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most scholars hold that bi-sm is an essential, intended part of the phrase.
rows.anchor: الجمهور إلى أن ( بسم ) أصل

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: The prefixed bāʾ has imperative force: begin in the name of God.
rows.anchor: الرحمن الرحيم وهذا قول الفراء

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The prefixed bāʾ has declarative force: I began in the name of God.
rows.anchor: الرحمن الرحيم وهذا قول الزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alif of connection is omitted in speech and writing through frequent use, as in al-Rahman; it remains written in 96:1 because that form is less frequent.
rows.anchor: اللفظ والخط , لكثرة الاستعمال كما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A name points to its referent, whereas an attribute conveys information about the one described; an attribute used as a name does both.
rows.anchor: المسمى دلالة إشارة , والصفة كلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that a name is identical with its referent and the spoken form is merely naming is unsound: it would make names of actions identical to the actions.
rows.anchor: كان أسماء الذوات هي الذوات

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He derives ism from sima, a mark, because a name distinguishes its referent.
rows.anchor: تمييز المسمى , وهذا قول الفراء

rows.speaker: الخليل والزجاج
rows.claim: They derive ism from elevation, because a name raises the person named above others.
rows.anchor: وهي الرفعة لأن الاسم يسمو

rows.speaker: عمرو بن معدي كرب
rows.claim: The cited verse witnesses the derivation of ism from elevation through the wording سما لك or سموت له.
rows.anchor: أمر سما لك أو سموت

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: He assigns symbolic meanings to the letters: bāʾ signifies beauty, blessing, goodness, and insight; sīn splendor, eminence, and mastery; mīm glory, dominion, and beneficence.
rows.anchor: والميم مجده ومملكته ومنه , وهذا قول الكلبي

rows.speaker: سليمان بن يسار
rows.claim: His letter symbolism says bāʾ means free of offspring, sīn hears voices, and mīm answers prayers.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول سليمان بن يسار

rows.speaker: أبو روق
rows.claim: His letter symbolism says bāʾ means creator, sīn concealer of faults, and mīm benefactor.
rows.anchor: السين ساتر العيوب , والميم المنان , وهذا قول أبي روق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The letter-symbol speculation is remote and exceeds what is proper for God's names, but he records it because an influential authority said it and the book collects reported views.
rows.anchor: الله تعالى به من أسمائه

rows.speaker: عمر بن أبي ربيعة
rows.claim: The poem uses basmala as a verb, evidence for the colloquial derived term basmala.
rows.anchor: قال عمر بن أبي ربيعة : لقد بسملت ليلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah is God's most particular name because no one besides Him has borne it.
rows.anchor: فهو أخص أسمائه به , لأنه لم يتسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation asks whether anyone comparable to Him is known; this is broader because it applies to both name and act.
rows.anchor: هل تعلم له شبيها , وهذا أعم التأويلين

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: He identifies Allah as the Greatest Name because no one shares this name.
rows.anchor: الاسم الأعظم من أسمائه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view treats Allah as a proper name for the divine essence, not derived from an attribute, since attribute names depend on an essence name.
rows.anchor: غير مشتق من صفاته , لأن أسماء الصفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view derives Allah from ilāh: the hamza is dropped and the pronunciation intensified.
rows.anchor: من أله , صار باشتقاقه عند حذف همزه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One etymology derives ilāh from yearning: creatures flee to Him in their affairs, as followers turn to an imam.
rows.anchor: من الوله , لأن العباد يألهون إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another etymology derives ilāh from ulūhiyya, worship, as in the verb meaning to worship.
rows.anchor: من الألوهية , وهي العبادة , من قولهم

rows.speaker: رؤبة بن العجاج
rows.claim: His poetic use of taʾalluh means worship and supports deriving ilāh from worship.
rows.anchor: 89 ( سبحن واسترجعن من تألهي ) 89

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He reportedly read 5:117 as wa-yadharuka wa-ālihataka, meaning your worship.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه قرأ : { ويذرك وءالهتك } أي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view derives ilāh from the act of worship, making divinity an attribute of action that began when creatures were created; on this view God was not always worshiped as ilāh.
rows.anchor: لا يكون ذلك صفة لازمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other view derives ilāh from deserving worship, making it an eternal essential attribute because God has always deserved worship.
rows.anchor: هذا يكون ذلك صفة لازمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers derivation from deserving worship: deriving it from the act would wrongly make Jesus and idols gods because people worshiped them.
rows.anchor: من فعل العبادة لا من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first derivation ilāh is an attribute of action; on the preferred derivation it is an attribute of the divine essence.
rows.anchor: القول صفة من صفات الذات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rahim is a divine name derived from His attribute of mercy.
rows.anchor: والرحيم فيها اسم مشتق من

rows.speaker: ثعلب
rows.claim: He regards al-Rahman as a foreignized Hebrew word, not Arabic, since eloquent Quraysh did not know it until it was explained to them in 25:60.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول ثعلب واستشهد بقول جرير

rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: His verse is cited as linguistic evidence for al-Rahman as an established name.
rows.anchor: ومسحكم صلبهم رحمن قربانا

rows.speaker: ثعلب
rows.claim: Pairing al-Rahman with al-Rahim removes ambiguity; on his theory the Arabic al-Rahim would originally come first, but al-Rahman is placed first for greater intensity.
rows.anchor: ليزول الالتباس , فعلى هذا يكون الأصل

rows.speaker: الشنفرى
rows.claim: His poem is cited as evidence that al-Rahman is used in Arabic speech and poetry.
rows.anchor: وقد ظهر ذلك في كلام العرب , وجاءت به أشعارهم , قال الشنفري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If both names are Arabic, they derive from mercy; mercy is a benefit to someone in need, and a benefit is called mercy because it arises from compassion.
rows.anchor: الرحمة , والرحمة هي النعمة على المحتاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase mercy to the worlds in 21:107 means a benefit to them, linking the verse's usage to this definition.
rows.anchor: يعني نعمة عليهم , وإنما سميت النعمة رحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rahman is more emphatic than al-Rahim: its form and meaning extend mercy, whereas al-Rahim extends only in meaning; people may be named Rahim but not Rahman.
rows.anchor: لأن الرحمن يتعدى لفظه ومعناه , والرحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pre-Islamic Arabs called God al-Rahman, and Musaylima later appropriated that divine name for himself.
rows.anchor: الله تعالى به وعليه بيت الشنفرى , ثم إن مسيلمة

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: He says al-Rahman was paired with al-Rahim to distinguish God's name through its intensity, since no one else called himself both names.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء : فلذلك قرنه الله تعالى بالرحيم

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: He distinguishes the names by saying al-Rahman is the possessor of mercy and al-Rahim is the merciful one.
rows.anchor: وفرق أبو عبيدة بينهما , فقال بأن الرحمن ذو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view derives al-Rahman and al-Rahim from the same mercy, with al-Rahman simply more emphatic.
rows.anchor: من رحمة واحدة , جعل لفظ الرحمن أشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view derives the names from two distinct mercies to distinguish the names and attributes.
rows.anchor: والرحمة التي اشتق منها الرحمن , غير الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account of the two mercies assigns al-Rahman to mercy toward all creatures and al-Rahim to mercy toward the obedient.
rows.anchor: رحمة الله لجميع خلقه , والرحيم مشتق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second account assigns al-Rahman to mercy for people of this world and the next, and al-Rahim to mercy for people of this world only.
rows.anchor: رحمة الله تعالى لأهل الدنيا والآخرة , والرحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third account assigns al-Rahman to mercy exclusive to God and al-Rahim to mercy that creatures can share.
rows.anchor: يختص الله تعالى بها دون عباده , والرحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamd praises a person for fine attributes and acts, while shukr praises for a blessing; every thanks is praise but not every praise is thanks, so God may praise Himself but not thank Himself.
rows.anchor: وأفعاله , والشكر الثناء عليه بإنعامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamd is deserved only for a good act, while madh may concern an act or a non-act; thus God may be praised for knowledge and power but not hamd for these essential attributes, while creation and provision merit both.
rows.anchor: قد يكون على فعل وغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One derivation of Rabb is owner, as in the owner of a house.
rows.anchor: أنه مشتق من المالك , كما يقال رب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another derives Rabb from master; in 12:41 the word refers to a person's master.
rows.anchor: السيد يسمى ربا قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third meaning of Rabb is manager, as scholars are called rabbaniyyun for managing people through knowledge.
rows.anchor: منه قول الله عز وجل : { والربانيون والأحبار } وهم العلماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth derivation is from nurturing or raising, as in the word for a wife's daughter raised in the household.
rows.anchor: الرب مشتق من التربية , ومنه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God Rabb as owner or master describes an essential attribute; calling Him Rabb as manager and nurturer describes action.
rows.anchor: لأنه مالك أو سيد , فذلك صفة من صفات ذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the definite article al-Rabb is exclusive to God; without it the word is shared by God and creatures.
rows.anchor: اختص الله تعالى به , دون عباده , وإن حذفتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀlamīn is a plural with no singular of the same form, like raht and qawm; people of each era form an ʿālam.
rows.anchor: لا واحد له من لفظه , مثل : رهط وقوم

rows.speaker: العجاج
rows.claim: The cited line using ʿālam witnesses the word's poetic use.
rows.anchor: وأهل كل زمان عالم قال العجاج :

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He defines the worlds as rational beings: angels, humans, and jinn.
rows.anchor: من الملائكة , والإنس , والجن , وهذا قول ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation makes the worlds this world and all that it contains.
rows.anchor: أن العالم الدنيا وما فيها

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق الزجاج
rows.claim: He defines the worlds as everything God created in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: الله تعالى في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If ʿālam means rational beings, the word derives from knowledge.
rows.anchor: أنه مشتق من العلم , وهذا تأويل من جعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If ʿālam means every creature, the word derives from sign because creation points to its Creator.
rows.anchor: لأنه دلالة على خالقه , وهذا تأويل من جعل

rows.speaker: عاصم والكسائي
rows.claim: They read malik, meaning Owner, while the other reciters read malik, meaning King.
rows.anchor: قرأ عاصم والكسائي { مالك } وقرأ الباقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One derivation of both readings links them to strength, as in strongly kneading dough.
rows.anchor: من الشدة , من قولهم ملكت العجين , إذا عجنته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another derivation links both readings to ability, as illustrated by the cited line about one's hand mastering a hole.
rows.anchor: من القدرة , قال الشاعر : ملكت بها كفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The owner has particular dominion, whereas the king has general dominion.
rows.anchor: أن المالك من كان خاص الملك , والملك من كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The owner possesses the property of kings, whereas the king possesses power to make commands effective.
rows.anchor: أن المالك من اختص بملك الملوك , والملك من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says King is greater praise: every king owns, not every owner is a king, and a king's command prevails over an owner's.
rows.anchor: الملك أبلغ في المدح من المالك , لأن كل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view says Owner is greater praise: one may rule Arabs or Romans without owning them, but an owner only owns what he possesses; kingship also covers people and other things.
rows.anchor: قد يكون ملكا على من

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: He says Owner better praises the Creator, while King better praises creatures; if God is owner He is also king, and the titles describe His acts and essence respectively.
rows.anchor: في مدح الخالق من ملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Describing God as King is an attribute of His essence; describing Him as Owner is an attribute of His acts.
rows.anchor: كان ذلك من صفات ذاته , وإن وصف بأنه مالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm al-din means either recompense or accounting.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : { يوم الدين } ففيه تأويلان

rows.speaker: المثقب العبدي
rows.claim: His verse uses dīn to mean custom or habitual practice.
rows.anchor: دينه أبدا وديني أي عادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another linguistic derivation of dīn is obedience, supported by Zuhayr's verse in the continuation.
rows.anchor: أن أصل الدين الطاعة , ومنه قول زهير بن أبي سلمى

rows.speaker: زهير بن أبي سلمى
rows.claim: His verse uses dīn to mean obedience to Amr.
rows.anchor: عمرو ومالت بيننا فدك أي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Judgment may be an ordinary day from dawn to sunset or a light that lasts until all creation has been judged and settled in Paradise or Hell.
rows.anchor: طلوع الفجر , وانتهاؤه غروب الشمس . والثاني : أنه ضياء

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: God alone rules on that Day, making His dominion greater than worldly kings' dominion.
rows.anchor: التي تملكها الملوك , وهذا قوله الأصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation pairs Lord of all worlds with King of the Day of Judgment to encompass rule of both this world and the next.
rows.anchor: قال بعده : { ملك يوم الدين } يريد به ملك الآخرة

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: He parses iyyaka as God's name annexed to the second-person suffix kāf.
rows.anchor: إلى الكاف , وهذا قول الخليل

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: He parses iyyaka as one word used as a pronoun for God, since a pronoun cannot be annexed.
rows.anchor: لأن المضمر لا يضاف , وهذا قول الأخفش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One meaning of worship is submission, the highest form of submission, due only to the giver of greatest blessings such as life and the senses.
rows.anchor: إلا الله تعالى , لأنها أعلى مراتب الخضوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second definition of worship is obedience.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أن العبادة الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third definition of worship is drawing near through obedience.
rows.anchor: والثالث : أنها التقرب بالطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The submission definition is clearest: Christians worshiped Jesus without obeying him, while the Prophet is obeyed but is not an object of worship.
rows.anchor: عبدَت عيسى عليه السلام , ولم تطعه بالعبادة , والنبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihdina can mean guide and show us the way.
rows.anchor: معناه أرشدنا ودلنا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He interprets ihdina as grant us success in following the way.
rows.anchor: معناه وفقنا , وهذا قول ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sirat can mean the straight path, as illustrated by Jarir's verse.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول جرير : أمير المؤمنين على صراط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sirat can also mean the clear road; the Quran and another poem use it this way, and its root is the passage of food through the throat.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله تعالى : ^ { ولا تقعدوا بكل صراط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer for guidance can seek its continuation even for people already guided.
rows.anchor: أنهم دعوا باستدامة الهداية , وإن كانوا قد هدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer can ask God to increase their guidance.
rows.anchor: معناه زدنا هداية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer can express sincere desire and hope for the reward of supplication.
rows.anchor: أنهم دعوا بها إخلاصا للرغبة , ورجاء لثواب الدعاء

rows.speaker: علي وعبد الله
rows.claim: They identify the straight path as God's Book; a similar interpretation is also transmitted from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وهو قول علي وعبد الله , ويروى نحوه عن النبي

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله ومحمد بن الحنفية
rows.claim: They identify the straight path as Islam.
rows.anchor: وهو قول جابر بن عبد الله , ومحمد بن الحنفية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He identifies it as the route that leads to God's religion and has no crookedness.
rows.anchor: الذي لا عوج فيه , وهو قول ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري وأبو العالية الرياحي
rows.claim: They identify the straight path as the Messenger and the best of his family and Companions.
rows.anchor: وسلم وأخيار أهل بيته وأصحابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those favored are variously identified as angels, prophets, believers in earlier scriptures, Muslims, or Muhammad and his Companions.
rows.anchor: { الذين أنعمت عليهم } خمسة أقاويل : أحدها : أنهم الملائكة

rows.speaker: وكيع
rows.claim: He identifies those favored as Muslims.
rows.anchor: أنهم المسلمون وهو قول وكيع

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
rows.claim: He identifies those favored as Muhammad and the Companions with him.
rows.anchor: قول عبد الرحمن بن زيد

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وعبد الله بن الزبير
rows.claim: They read sirat man anʿamta ʿalayhim instead of sirat alladhina anʿamta ʿalayhim.
rows.anchor: عمر بن الخطاب وعبد الله بن الزبير

rows.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
rows.claim: He asked the Prophet who the angered and astray groups were; the Prophet identified them as Jews and Christians, respectively, as all exegetes agree.
rows.anchor: عن عدي بن حاتم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account understands divine anger as the anger known among human beings.
rows.anchor: الغضب المعروف من العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second account interprets God's anger as a will to punish; anger linguistically means severity, a quality unsuitable for God.
rows.anchor: في اللغة هو الغلظة , وهذه الصفة لا تجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third account interprets God's anger as His condemnation of them.
rows.anchor: أن غضبه عليهم هو ذمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth account calls a kind of punishment anger, just as God's bounty is called mercy.
rows.anchor: نوع من العقوبة سمي غضبا , كما سميت نعمه رحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Misguidance is the opposite of guidance, and Jews are singled out for anger because they are more intensely hostile.
rows.anchor: وخص الله تعالى اليهود بالغضب

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: He read the closing phrase with a repeated ghayr before wa-la al-dallin.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن الخطاب ( غير المغضوب عليهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
rows.claim: They understand sabbih as magnify your Lord; ism is an extra word intended to magnify the one named, as in Labid's poem.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عباس والسدي , والاسم صلة قصد

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: His verse is cited as poetic evidence for using ism as an extra word in praise.
rows.anchor: كما قال لبيد : إلى الحول ثم اسم السلام عليكما

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: He interprets the command as keeping the name of the Lord from being applied to anyone else.
rows.anchor: يسمى به أحد سواه , ذكره الطبري

rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: His line supports the interpretation of sabbih as raising one's voice in remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: قال جرير : قبح الإله وجوه تغلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth interpretation is pray to your Lord; ism may mean by His command, by remembering Him at prayer's opening, or remembering Him in the heart when intending prayer.
rows.anchor: في قوله ( اسم ربك ) ثلاثة أوجه : أحدها

rows.speaker: علي وابن عباس وابن عمر
rows.claim: They reportedly began reciting the sura by saying Subhana rabbi al-aʿla, acting on its opening command; Abu's recitation and Ibn Umar's reading included the formula.
rows.anchor: عمر كانوا إذا افتتحوا قراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is that God created people and then perfected them.
rows.anchor: يعني أنشأ خلقهم ثم سواهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation is that God created people complete and made each limb correspond to its proper counterpart.
rows.anchor: خلقا كاملا وسوى لكل جارحة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: He says God created Adam and perfected his form.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك : خلق آدم فسوى خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third possible reading is that God created people through His beneficence and made their rulings equal.
rows.anchor: خلقهم بإنعامه وسوى بينهم في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation places creation in men's loins and proportioning in mothers' wombs.
rows.anchor: خلق في أصلاب الرجال , وسوى في أرحام الأمهات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation distinguishes creation of bodies from proportioning of understandings.
rows.anchor: خلق الأجساد فسوى الأفهام

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He says God decreed wretchedness and happiness and guided people to right guidance or error.
rows.anchor: وهداه للرشد والضلالة , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation says God determined people's provisions and guided humans to livelihoods and animals to pasture.
rows.anchor: وهداهم لمعاشهم إن كانوا إنسا

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: He says God determined male and female and guided the male in how to approach the female.
rows.anchor: كيف يأتى الأنثى , قاله السدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possibility is that God determined their creation in the womb and guided them to emerge fully formed.
rows.anchor: قدر خلقهم في الأرحام , وهداهم الخروج للتمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is that God created people for recompense and guided them to action.
rows.anchor: خلقهم للجزاء , وهداهم للعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited verse says pasture sprouts over the soil of ruins, with grief remaining in human hearts.
rows.anchor: وقد ينبت المرعى على دمن الثرى … وتبقى حزازات النفوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poem describes vegetation growing over the dust of ruins.
rows.anchor: المرعى على دمن الثرى … وتبقى حزازات النفوس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Ghutha is dried, brittle vegetation scattered by the wind, and ahwa means black; Dhu al-Rumma's verse supports the color sense.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى قول مجاهد . الثاني : أن الغثاء ما

rows.speaker: ذي الرمة
rows.claim: His verse uses ḥawa for dark coloring of lips and related features.
rows.anchor: شفتيها حوة لعس وفي اللثات

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: He says ghutha is plants carried by a flood and ahwa means changed in color.
rows.anchor: المتغير , وهذا معنى قول السدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading uses reversed order: ahwa describes the living plant's colors before it becomes ghutha; all those colors may be called black, as in Sawad Iraq.
rows.anchor: ومعناه أحوى فصار غثاء , والأحوى : ألوان النبات

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: His line is cited as evidence for the term ahwa describing dark vegetation.
rows.anchor: وقال امرؤ القيس : وغيث دائم التهتا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He interprets purification as clearing oneself of idolatry through faith.
rows.anchor: من تطهر من الشرك بالإيمان , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن والربيع
rows.claim: They interpret it as righteous deeds becoming pure and growing.
rows.anchor: زكيا ناميا , قاله الحسن والربيع

rows.speaker: أبو الأحوص
rows.claim: He interprets the verse as referring to all obligatory wealth alms.
rows.anchor: زكاة الأموال كلها , قاله أبو الأحوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible meaning is a person who increases in goodness and righteousness.
rows.anchor: أنه من ازداد خيرا وصلاحا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He interprets remembering the Lord's name as affirming God's unity.
rows.anchor: أن يوحد الله , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another meaning is calling upon God and directing one's desire to Him.
rows.anchor: أن يدعوه ويرغب إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another meaning is seeking forgiveness and repenting to God.
rows.anchor: أن يستغفروه ويتوب إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is inward recollection during prayer, producing fear of punishment and hope for reward, and therefore full attention and humility.
rows.anchor: صلاته فيخاف عقابه ويرجو ثوابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is verbally mentioning God's name at the start of prayer, since prayer is not valid without it.
rows.anchor: بصلاته , لأنها لا تنعقد إلا بذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation is opening each sura with the basmala.
rows.anchor: يفتتح كل سورة ببسم الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He says fa-salla refers to the five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: الصلوات الخمس , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: He says fa-salla refers to the Eid prayer.
rows.anchor: صلاة العيد , قاله أبو سعيد الخدري

rows.speaker: أبو الأحوص
rows.claim: He interprets it as performing a voluntary prayer after paying alms.
rows.anchor: يتطوع بصلاة بعد زكاة , قاله أبو الأحوص

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: He reports that the sura was revealed concerning Abu Bakr.
rows.anchor: وذكر الضحاك أنها نزلت في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view addresses unbelievers: they prefer worldly life to the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أن المراد بها الكفار , فيكون تأويلها : بل تؤثرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view addresses Muslims: they prefer accumulating worldly goods to accumulating reward.
rows.anchor: أن المراد بها المسلمون , فيكون تأويلها : يؤثرون الاستكثار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading says the afterlife is better for believers than worldly life and its recompense lasts longer.
rows.anchor: خير للمؤمن من الدنيا , وأبقى للجزاء

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He reads the comparison as better in goodness and more lasting in permanence.
rows.anchor: ما قاله قتادة خير في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that the afterlife is better for the obedient and more lasting for the people of Paradise.
rows.anchor: خير لأهل الطاعة وأبقى على

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He says the afterlife's superiority and permanence already appear in earlier scriptures.
rows.anchor: خير وأبقى في الصحف الأولى ، قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view says all that God recounted in this sura comes from earlier scriptures.
rows.anchor: الله في هذه السورة هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view identifies the earlier scriptures as all of God's revealed books; Wahb ibn Munabbih reports their count and distribution among the prophets.
rows.anchor: بن منبه في المبتدإ أن

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: He reports 105 scrolls and four books: 35 scrolls for Seth, 50 for Enoch, 20 for Abraham, and the Torah, Psalms, Gospel, and Furqan for Moses, David, Jesus, and Muhammad.
rows.anchor: خمسة وثلاثون صحيفة أنزلها على

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
rows.claim: They identify al-ghāshiya as the Resurrection, which envelops people with terrors.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عباس والضحاك . الثاني : أنها النار

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: He identifies al-ghāshiya as the Fire, which envelops unbelievers' faces.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن جبير . ويحتمل ثالثا : أنها في هذا الموضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is the blast of resurrection, because it envelops all creatures.
rows.anchor: الموضع النفخة الثانية للبعث لأنها

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: He treats hal as equivalent to qad, so the phrase means the report has indeed reached you.
rows.anchor: قد أتاك حديث الغاشية ، قاله قطرب . الثاني

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: He takes hal as an interrogative addressed to the Messenger, meaning: had the report not reached you? It has.
rows.anchor: خرجت مخرج الاستفهام لرسوله ، ومعناه ألم يكن قد أتاك

rows.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
rows.claim: He says the faces are those of all unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وجوه الكفار كلهم , قاله يحيى بن سلام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He says the faces belong to Jews and Christians.
rows.anchor: وجوه اليهود والنصارى , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: He interprets yawm idhin as the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: يعني يوم القيامة , قاله سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He interprets yawm idhin as the Fire.
rows.anchor: في النار , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He says the faces are humbled by their sins.
rows.anchor: يعني ذليلة بمعاصيها , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: He says they will be humbled after punishment and deprived of enjoyment.
rows.anchor: فلا تتنعم , قاله سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that they display obedience after admitting their disobedience.
rows.anchor: تكون خاشعة لتظاهرها بطاعته بعد

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: He says they worked in disobedience during worldly life.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا عاملة بالمعاصي , قاله عكرمة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He says they arrogantly refused God's obedience in life, so in Hell they are made to labor by moving from one punishment to another.
rows.anchor: من عذاب إلى عذاب , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that, if returned to life, they would expend themselves in obedience.
rows.anchor: أي باذلة للعمل بطاعته إن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation of nāṣiba is laboring in sinful deeds.
rows.anchor: ناصبة في أعمال المعاصي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He interprets nāṣiba as exhausted in the Fire.
rows.anchor: ناصبة في النار ، قاله قتادة . ويحتمل وجها ثالثا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is standing before God and seeking refuge in His pardon.
rows.anchor: ناصبة بين يديه تعالى مستجيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although hot is a minimal description of Fire, the verse's intensity can refer to heat that never ends as earthly fire does.
rows.anchor: دائمة الحمى وليست كنار الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading uses ḥāmiya for a protected sanctuary that deters violations, by analogy with the Prophet's statement that God's sanctuary is His prohibitions.
rows.anchor: من ارتكاب المحظورات وانتهاك المحارم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading says the Fire protects itself from being touched or approached as a lion guards its den.
rows.anchor: أن تطاق ملامستها أو ترام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author introduces al-Nabigha verse as an analogy for the Fire guarding itself like a lion guarding its den.
rows.anchor: كما يحي الأسد عرينه , ومثله قول النابغة :

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: He gives an interpretation of āniya, though the excerpt does not preserve its wording.
rows.anchor: فيه أربعة أوجه : أحدها : قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation of āniya is present or at hand.
rows.anchor: الثاني : حاضرة .

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He says the spring has reached its full point and is ready to be drunk.
rows.anchor: وحان شربها , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He says the heat has come to its end and grown intense.
rows.anchor: قد أنى حرها فانتهى واشتد , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He identifies ḍarīʿ as the thorny shrub Quraysh call shibrq.
rows.anchor: كثيرة الشوك , قاله ابن عباس , قال قتادة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He says the shrub is called ḍarīʿ when it dries in summer; the poem describes fresh shibrq becoming ḍarīʿ and camels disputing over it.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة وإذا يبس في

rows.speaker: أبو الجوزاء
rows.claim: He identifies it as the thorny salm shrub and asks how anyone could gain nourishment from eating thorns.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الجوزاء : كيف يسمن من يأكل الشوك

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: He says ḍarīʿ means stones.
rows.anchor: أنها الحجارة , قاله ابن جبير

rows.speaker: يوسف بن يعقوب
rows.claim: He transmits from an unnamed Bedouin that ḍarīʿ is burnt date stones.
rows.anchor: حكاه يوسف بن يعقوب عن

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: He identifies ḍarīʿ as a tree made of fire.
rows.anchor: أنه شجر من نار , قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: He derives the word from people crying out for deliverance from it.
rows.anchor: يضرعون عنده طلبا للخلاص منه , قاله ابن بحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth reading makes the Fire hot from wrath and anger, an intensification of vengeance, as 67:8 says it nearly bursts with rage.
rows.anchor: الرابع : أنها حامية مما غيظ وغضب , مبالغة في شدة الانتقام , وقد بين الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited al-Nabigha verse describes wolves avoiding the fierce lion, illustrating the Fire protecting itself from approach.
rows.anchor: تعدو الذئاب على من لا كلاب له … وتتقي صولة المستأسد الحامي

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: He says the garden is high because it stands above the Fire.
rows.anchor: فسميت لذلك عالية , قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation places the garden's upper levels and chambers in the high and elevated parts.
rows.anchor: أعالي الجنة وغرقها , لأنها منازل العلو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their elevation may provide delight or let residents see the blessings prepared for them.
rows.anchor: الثاني : ليشاهدوا ما أعد الله لهم فيها

rows.speaker: الفراء والأخفش
rows.claim: They explain laghiya as a word of idle talk.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء والأخفش : أي لا تسمع فيها كلمة لغو

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He says laghiya means a lie.
rows.anchor: يعني كذبا , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He says laghiya means sin.
rows.anchor: الثاني : الإثم , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He says laghiya means abusive speech.
rows.anchor: الثالث : أنه الشتم , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
rows.claim: He says laghiya means falsehood or vanity.
rows.anchor: الرابع : الباطل , قاله يحيى بن سلام

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He says laghiya means disobedience.
rows.anchor: الخامس : المعصية , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: He says no one in Paradise swears, whether a true or false oath.
rows.anchor: في الجنة حالف يمين برة ولا فاجرة , قاله الكلبي

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He says no word in their speech is dismissed as useless, because they speak only wisdom and praise God for what He provided.
rows.anchor: لأن أهل الجنة لا يتكلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Surur is the plural of sarir, a couch, a word derived from delight.
rows.anchor: والسرر جمع سرير , وهو مشتق من السرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raised couches may be tiered, exalted in the residents' esteem, or elevated in place.
rows.anchor: وفي وصفها بأنها مرفوعة ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He says the couches are raised in the residents' eyes because of their grandeur and their love for them.
rows.anchor: لجلالتها وحبهم لها , قاله الفراء

rows.speaker: ابن شجرة
rows.claim: One purpose of elevated couches is to give residents enjoyment.
rows.anchor: بارتفاعها , قاله ابن شجرة . الثاني : ليشاهدوا

rows.speaker: ابن عيسى
rows.claim: Another purpose is to let residents see the kingdom and blessings they have received.
rows.anchor: من نعيم , قاله ابن عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akwāb are vessels or cups.
rows.anchor: فالأكواب : الأواني , وقد مضى القول في تفسيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cups may be placed in their hands so they can enjoy looking at the gold and silver vessels.
rows.anchor: للاستمتاع بالنظر إليها لأنها من

rows.speaker: المفضل
rows.claim: He says the cups are continuously in use because drinking from them continues without interruption.
rows.anchor: استدامة شربهم منها , قاله المفضل

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He identifies namāriq as cushions or pillows, singular nimriqa.
rows.anchor: الوسائد , واحدها نمرقة , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن أبي طلحة
rows.claim: He identifies namāriq as armrests.
rows.anchor: المرافق , قاله ابن أبي طلحة , قال الشاعر :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author introduces a poem illustrating the word namāriq at the end of this segment.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن أبي طلحة , قال الشاعر :

rows.speaker: ابن عيسى
rows.claim: He identifies zarābī as luxurious carpets.
rows.anchor: هي البسط الفاخرة ، قاله ابن عيسى

rows.speaker: الكلبي والفراء
rows.claim: They identify zarābī as plush velvet rugs.
rows.anchor: هي الطنافس المخملة ، قاله الكلبي والفراء

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He interprets mabthūtha as spread out.
rows.anchor: أحدها : مبسوطة ، قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: He interprets mabthūtha as layered, one above another.
rows.anchor: الثاني : بعضها فوق بعض ، قاله عكرمة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He interprets mabthūtha as numerous.
rows.anchor: الثالث : الكثيرة ، قاله الفراء

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: He interprets mabthūtha as scattered or dispersed.
rows.anchor: الرابع : المتفرقة ، قاله ابن قتيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning the camel, sky, mountains, and earth invites people to infer God's power and unity from their signs.
rows.anchor: فيها من العبر على قدره

rows.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
rows.claim: The signs also show God's power to resurrect people on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: بعثهم يوم القيامة , قاله يحيى بن سلام

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: After misguided people marveled at Paradise, these earthly marvels are mentioned to remove their astonishment.
rows.anchor: الجنة عجب منه أهل الضلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The more obvious and common meaning of al-ibil is domestic camels, though another view reads it as clouds.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : وهو أظهرهما وأشهرهما : أنها الإبل من النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If al-ibil means clouds, they display signs of divine power and benefits shared by all creatures.
rows.anchor: فيها من الآيات الدالة على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If it means livestock camels, they combine milk, riding, food, and carrying, more kinds of benefit than other animals and a clearer display of power.
rows.anchor: ضروبه أربعة : حلوبة , وركوبة , وأكولة , وحمولة والإبل تجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-dhakkir means preach or admonish.
rows.anchor: إنما أنت واعظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is to remind them of blessings so they fear punishments.
rows.anchor: ذكرهم النعم ليخافوا النقم

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: He interprets musaytir as someone with power or authority over them.
rows.anchor: لست عليهم بمسلط , قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He interprets musaytir as a tyrant or coercive ruler.
rows.anchor: الثاني : بجبار , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He interprets musaytir as a lord or master.
rows.anchor: الثالث : برب , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger cannot force people to believe.
rows.anchor: أن تكرههم على الإيمان

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: The Messenger cannot admonish those who turn away and disbelieve, because they will not accept his reminder.
rows.anchor: لأنه لا يقبل تذكيرك , قاله السدي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Another view says to leave those who turn away and disbelieve to God; this was before fighting was commanded.
rows.anchor: ثم أمر بقتالهم , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawalla wa-kafara may mean turning from truth and disbelieving the blessing.
rows.anchor: تولى عن الحق وكفر بالنعمة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: He reads it as turning away from the Messenger and disbelieving in God.
rows.anchor: تولى عن الرسول وكفر بالله تعالى , قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greater punishment is Hell; it may also mean remaining there forever, which is greater than a finite punishment.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد الخلود فيها , لأنه يصير بالاستدامة أكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their return is to God.
rows.anchor: { إن إلينا إيابهم } أي مرجعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their accounting means recompense for their deeds, combining promise and threat through reward for obedience and punishment for sins.
rows.anchor: جزاءهم على أعمالهم , فيكون ذلك جامعا بين الوعد والوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The segment opens with a poetic fragment comparing Iram's fall to sleepers' dreams; its referent is unclear in the excerpt.
rows.anchor: كما سخرت به إرم فأضحوا … مثل أحلام النيام

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: One interpretation treats Iram as the name of a tribe of ʿĀd.
rows.anchor: أنه اسم قبيلة من عاد , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: He says Iram was the ancestor of ʿĀd; another report from him calls Iram their father and gives the lineage as ʿĀd son of Iram son of ʿAwḍ son of Shem son of Noah.
rows.anchor: قاله محمد بن إسحاق , وحكى عنه أنه أبوه

rows.speaker: ابن أبي نجيح
rows.claim: A transmitted interpretation understands Iram as ancient.
rows.anchor: أن معنى إرم القديمة , رواه ابن أبي نجيح

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: He derives Iram from destruction, as in the expression that a people perished.
rows.anchor: أرم بنو فلان , أي هلكوا , قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: He says God crushed them into remains, giving them the name Iram.
rows.anchor: فجعلهم رميما , فلذلك سماهم , قاله السدي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He derives dhāt al-ʿimād from their great height; Qatada says one of their men stood twelve cubits tall.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس مأخوذ من

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He says they were people of tents and poles who traveled seeking rain.
rows.anchor: أهل خيام وأعمدة , ينتجعون الغيوث , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He reports that one of their men was twelve cubits tall.
rows.anchor: وزعم قتادة . أنه كان طول الرجل منهم

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: He derives the phrase from strength and might, like the strength of sturdy pillars.
rows.anchor: مأخوذ من قوة الأعمدة , قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: ثور بن يزيد
rows.claim: He relates a boast attributed to Shaddad son of ʿĀd about raising the pillar, bending his arm, and a buried treasure only Muhammad's nation could recover.
rows.anchor: وحكى ثور بن يزيد أنه

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: He understands dhāt al-ʿimād as securely fastened with pillars.
rows.anchor: ذات العماد المحكم بالعماد , قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: He says no city like Iram, with its pillars, was created in the lands.
rows.anchor: لم يخلق مثل مدينتهم ذات العماد في البلاد , قاله عكرمة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He says no people like ʿĀd were created in the lands because of their height and strength.
rows.anchor: لم يخلق مثل قوم عاد في البلاد , لطولهم وشدتهم , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading says Thamud cut and hollowed out rock to make houses, as 26:149 also says.
rows.anchor: حتى جعلوه بيوتا , كما قال تعالى : { وتنحتون من الجبال بيوتا

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The cited poem describes striking a solid rock with strong arms, supporting the reading that Thamud hewed stone.
rows.anchor: وهم ضربوا في كل صماء صعدة … بأيد شديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading says they traveled around the valley to obtain stone.
rows.anchor: معناه طافوا لأخذ الصخر بالوادي

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: He identifies the wadi as Wadi al-Qura.
rows.anchor: زعم محمد بن إسحاق أنه

rows.speaker: أبو الأشهب عن أبي نضرة
rows.claim: They report that during the Tabuk campaign the Prophet passed through the valley of Thamud on a gray horse and ordered the group to hurry because it was cursed.
rows.anchor: أبو الأشهب عن أبي نضرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He says Pharaoh's pegs were his numerous troops.
rows.anchor: لكثرة جنوده , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
rows.claim: They say Pharaoh tortured people by fastening stakes to their hands; al-Kalbi adds that Pharaoh tortured his believing wife Asiya this way until she died.
rows.anchor: قاله الحسن , ومجاهد , قال الكلبي : بمثل ذلك

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: He says the pegs were buildings, and Pharaoh was called this because he built many of them.
rows.anchor: لكثرة بنائه , قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He says Pharaoh had tents and amusements supported by pegs and ropes, under which games were played.
rows.anchor: يلعب له تحتها , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that the title refers to abundant palm trees and other trees rooted like pegs.
rows.anchor: لكثرة نخله وشجره , لأنها كالأوتاد في الأرض

rows.speaker: ابن عيسى
rows.claim: One interpretation of sawṭ al-ʿadhāb is a portion of punishment like a lash's punishment.
rows.anchor: كالعذاب بالسوط , قاله ابن عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites an unnamed poetic line about blood mixing to illustrate the interpretation of sawt as mixed punishment.
rows.anchor: أحارث إنا لو تساط دماؤنا … تزيلن حتى لا يمس دم دما

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: He interprets sawṭ al-ʿadhāb as pain from punishment.
rows.anchor: أنه وجع من العذاب , قاله السدي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He says sawṭ al-ʿadhāb means anything by which God punishes, and identifies it here as drowning.
rows.anchor: فهو سوط عذاب , قاله قتادة . وقال قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mirṣād can mean the road or a state of waiting and watching, the latter supported by Ṭarafa's poem.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : بالطريق . الثاني : بالانتظار , كما قال طرفة :

rows.speaker: طرفة
rows.claim: His verse uses the word mursaḍ for a place where death waits for men.
rows.anchor: وإن المنايا للرجال بمرصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turāth means inheritance.
rows.anchor: والتراث : الميراث , وفي قوله ( لما ) أربعة تأويلات

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: He interprets lamman as eating intensely or greedily.
rows.anchor: يعني شديدا , قاله السدي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He interprets lamman as collecting and eating things together.
rows.anchor: إذا أكلته جمعا , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He explains it as heedlessly devouring the inheritance.
rows.anchor: معناه سفه سفا , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: He says a person who consumes his own inheritance also takes others' property, without distinguishing forbidden from permitted wealth.
rows.anchor: بمال غيره فأكله , ولا يتفكر فيما أكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that the person gathers what was forbidden and withheld from him.
rows.anchor: ألم بما حرم عليه ومنع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He interprets loving wealth jamman as loving it abundantly.
rows.anchor: يعني كثيرا , قاله ابن عباس , والجم الكثير

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The poem uses jamman to mean plentifully.
rows.anchor: إن تغفر اللهم تغفر جما … وأي عبد لك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He calls the love excessive: people combine lawful wealth with unlawful wealth.
rows.anchor: تجمعون حلاله إلى حرامه , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is loving money only to stockpile it, using it for neither religious nor worldly benefit, the worst state for a wealthy person.
rows.anchor: فلا ينتفع به في دين

rows.speaker: ابن أبي نجيح
rows.claim: He transmits the cited poem about a person contending amid hardship, as evidence for the meaning of fi kabad.
rows.anchor: في كبد . رواه ابن أبي نجيح . الخامس

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He says a person struggles with worldly disasters and the hardships of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: مصائب الدنيا وشدائد الآخرة , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: He says Adam was created in the middle of the sky.
rows.anchor: خلق آدم في كبد السماء , قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: He says people must struggle to give thanks in prosperity and patience in adversity, since they always face one or the other.
rows.anchor: لأنه لا يخلو من أحدهما , رواه ابن عمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that the human being is fierce and proud, from an expression for someone strongly defensive and proud.
rows.anchor: ذو نفور وحمية , مأخوذ من قولهم لفلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human addressed may mean everyone, or specifically an unbeliever contending with doubts.
rows.anchor: ها هنا قولان : أحدهما : جميع الناس . الثاني : الكافر

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: He reads the question as whether a person thinks God cannot resurrect him after death.
rows.anchor: أن لن يقدر عليه الله أن يبعثه بعد الموت , قاله السدي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He reads it as whether anyone can take away the person's wealth.
rows.anchor: أحد بأخذ ماله , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading asks whether a person thinks no one can humiliate him, since being overpowered entails humiliation.
rows.anchor: أيحسب أن لن يذله أحد , لأن القدرة عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Labadan may mean a large amount of money.
rows.anchor: لبدا } فيه وجهان : أحدهما : يعني كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Labadan may mean piled together, like felt, because the wealth is packed one layer on another.
rows.anchor: مجتمعا بعضه على بعض , ومنه سمي اللبد لاجتماعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third possibility is old wealth, deriving the word from abad or from the proverbically ancient Lubad, emphasizing how long it was hoarded.
rows.anchor: لاشتقاقه من الأبد , أو للمبالغة في قدمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker may be Abu al-Ashadd al-Jumahi, who spent much wealth opposing the Messenger and God's path, or al-Nadr ibn al-Harith.
rows.anchor: كثيرا في عداوة رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His statement may boast of extravagant spending and thus show insolence, or lament the loss and show regret.
rows.anchor: فيكون طغيانا منه . الثاني : أن يكون أسفا عليه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He says the person thinks God did not see what he spent.
rows.anchor: أن لم يره الله , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن شجرة
rows.claim: He says the person thinks no one among people saw what he spent.
rows.anchor: فيما أنفقه , قاله ابن شجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reading is a threat: the person thinks no one will expose or punish what he did; the other readings refute his claim.
rows.anchor: ما فعله أن لا يؤاخذ

rows.speaker: علي والحسن
rows.claim: They identify the two paths as good and evil.
rows.anchor: سبيل الخير والشر , قاله علي رضي الله عنه والحسن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He identifies them as guidance and misguidance.
rows.anchor: سبيل الهدى والضلالة , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He identifies them as misery and happiness.
rows.anchor: سبيل الشقاء والسعادة , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: قتادة والربيع بن خثيم
rows.claim: They identify the two peaks as the two breasts by which an infant is nourished.
rows.anchor: قاله قتادة والربيع بن خثيم

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: He defines najd as a high road, distinguishing elevated Najd from low-lying Tihama.
rows.anchor: والنجد هو الطريق المرتفع , فأرض نجد هي المرتفعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under the high-road derivation, the two peaks could be Paradise and Fire because they rise above the earth.
rows.anchor: أنهما الجنة والنار , لارتفاعهما عن الأرض

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He interprets the oath as swearing by the sky and its construction.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : والسماء وبنائها , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: مجاهد والحسن
rows.claim: They interpret it as swearing by the sky and the One who built it, God.
rows.anchor: ومن بناها وهو الله تعالى , قاله مجاهد والحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third possibility is swearing by what is in the sky's construction, such as angels and stars, in contrast to what precedes as an oath by earthly things.
rows.anchor: يعني من الملائكة والنجوم , فيكون هذا قسما بما في السماء

rows.speaker: سفيان وأبو صالح
rows.claim: They interpret taḥāhā as spread or flattened the earth.
rows.anchor: معناه بسطها , قاله سفيان وأبو صالح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He interprets taḥāhā as divided the earth.
rows.anchor: معناه قسمها , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: عطية العوفي
rows.claim: He interprets it as what God created in the earth, understanding taḥāhā to mean created it.
rows.anchor: ما خلق فيها , قاله عطية العوفي , ويكون طحاها

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The line about Jadhima not knowing who created or spread the earth witnesses the verb ṭaḥā.
rows.anchor: وما تدري جذيمة من طحاها … ولا من ساكن العرش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reading includes plants, springs, and treasures emerging from the earth, sustaining life on it.
rows.anchor: من نبات وعيون وكنوز , لأنه حياة لما خلق عليها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: One view identifies the soul as Adam and its fashioner as God.
rows.anchor: ومن سواها : الله تعالى , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view understands the soul as every soul.
rows.anchor: أنها كل نفس

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: On the universal-soul view, God made people equal in health and equal in punishment.
rows.anchor: وسوى بينهم في العذاب جميعا , قاله ابن جريج

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: On the universal-soul view, God proportioned and balanced the soul's creation.
rows.anchor: سوى خلقها وعدل خلقها , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that God endowed the soul with intellect, distinguishing it from all animals.
rows.anchor: بالعقل الذي فضلها به على

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He interprets alhamaha as making the soul know its choices.
rows.anchor: أعلمها , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: He interprets alhamaha as compelling or binding the soul to its course.
rows.anchor: ألزمها , قاله ابن جبير

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He interprets its wickedness and piety as misery and happiness.
rows.anchor: الشقاء والسعادة , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He interprets them as evil and good.
rows.anchor: الشر والخير , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: He interprets them as obedience and disobedience.
rows.anchor: الطاعة والمعصية , قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that fear and hope are the motives that lead to wickedness and piety.
rows.anchor: الرهبة والرغبة لأنهما داعيا الفجور

rows.speaker: جوبير عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: They transmit that when the Prophet recited this verse, he raised his voice in prayer asking God to grant his soul piety and purify it.
rows.anchor: جوبير عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He says the oath concludes here and counts eleven oaths in the passage.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : فيها أحد عشر قسما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading says God purified the soul through obedience and good deeds.
rows.anchor: من زكى الله نفسه بطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading says the person purified his own soul through obedience and good deeds.
rows.anchor: من زكى نفسه بطاعة الله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He interprets zakkāhā as purified it.
rows.anchor: طهرها , وهو قول مجاهد

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: He interprets zakkāhā as improved or reformed it.
rows.anchor: وهو قول سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading says a person failed by God's decree in the way He made the soul corrupt; another says the person corrupted his own soul.
rows.anchor: خاب من دسى الله نفسه

rows.speaker: مجاهد وسعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: They interpret dassāhā as misleading or leading the soul astray by sinking it into sins.
rows.anchor: قاله مجاهد وسعيد بن جبير , لأنه دسى نفسه

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: They interpret ṭaghwāhā as Thamud's tyranny and disobedience.
rows.anchor: بطغيانها ومعصيتها , قاله مجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: He interprets the phrase as referring to all of Thamud collectively.
rows.anchor: بأجمعها , قاله محمد بن كعب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He says ṭaghwāhā was the name of the punishment that struck Thamud.
rows.anchor: بعذابها , قاله ابن عباس . قالوا كان اسم العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Damdama may mean He became angry with them.
rows.anchor: معناه فغضب عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Damdama may mean He enclosed or encompassed them.
rows.anchor: معناه فأطبق عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Damdama may mean He destroyed them; the word is of Abyssinian origin adopted into Arabic.
rows.anchor: وهو مثل دمدم , كلمة بالحبشية نطقت بها العرب

rows.speaker: السدي ويحيى بن سلام
rows.claim: They interpret fa-sawwāhā as making them equal in destruction.
rows.anchor: قاله السدي ويحيى بن سلام

rows.speaker: ابن شجرة
rows.claim: He interprets it as leveling them with the earth.
rows.anchor: فسوى بهم الأرض , ذكره ابن شجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that God leveled later nations after them.
rows.anchor: فسوى من بعدهم من الأمم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He says God does not fear the consequence of destroying them.
rows.anchor: ما صنع بهم من الهلاك , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He says the person who hamstrung the she-camel does not fear the consequence of the deed.
rows.anchor: ما صنع من عقرها , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that Salih did not fear the consequence because he had warned them and God rescued him when they were destroyed.
rows.anchor: ولا يخاف صالح عقبى عقرها , لأنه قد أنذرهم

rows.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
rows.claim: He says God undertook to make the paths of guidance and error clear.
rows.anchor: والضلالة قاله يحيى بن سلام

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He interprets guidance as explaining what is lawful and unlawful.
rows.anchor: بيان الحلال والحرام , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that God undertakes the reward for the guidance He has given.
rows.anchor: علينا ثواب هداه الذي هدينا

rows.speaker: الكلبي والفراء
rows.claim: They interpret the first and last lives as the rewards of this world and the next.
rows.anchor: ثواب الدنيا والآخرة , قاله الكلبي والفراء

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: He interprets the verse as God's dominion over this world and the next.
rows.anchor: ملك الدنيا وملك الآخرة , قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reading says God recompenses people in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: الله المجازي في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: He interprets talazzā as seething with anger.
rows.anchor: معناه تتغيظ , قاله الكلبي

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: He interprets talazzā as catching fire.
rows.anchor: تشتعل , قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He interprets talazzā as glowing intensely; Ali's poem illustrates the word.
rows.anchor: تتوهج , قاله مجاهد , وأنشد لعلي رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: His verse compares a glowing fire to salt mixed into something and shining like agate in shade.
rows.anchor: كأن الملح خالطه إذا ما … تلظى كالعقيقة في الظلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ashqā means the wretched person.
rows.anchor: إلا الأشقى } أي الشقي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He says the person lied about God's Book and turned away from God's obedience.
rows.anchor: وتولى عن طاعة الله , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation says the person lied about the Messenger and turned away from obeying him.
rows.anchor: كذب الرسول وتولى عن طاعته

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: One reading says no one at God's side has a favor to repay: rather, perform an act seeking God's face and earn its reward.
rows.anchor: عليها الجزاء والثواب , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
rows.claim: They apply the verse to Bilal: Abu Bakr's purchase and freeing of him repaid no prior favor; he acted only to seek God's face.
rows.anchor: من الرق وخلصه من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised satisfaction may come from the abundance of what is given or from being content with what is given, since a content person obeys God more.
rows.anchor: بما أعطيه لقناعته , لأن من قنع بغير عطاء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He reports that the Prophet was shown the conquests his community would make and rejoiced, after which this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: روى ابن عباس قال : عرض على رسول الله

rows.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
rows.claim: He says the afterlife is better for the Prophet than what delighted him in worldly life.
rows.anchor: أعجبك في الدنيا , قاله يحيى بن سلام

rows.speaker: ابن شجرة
rows.claim: He says the Prophet's ultimate return to God will be greater than the worldly honor already given him.
rows.anchor: من كرامة الدنيا , قاله ابن شجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may give the Prophet victory in this world and make the religion manifest, satisfying him.
rows.anchor: يعطيك من النصر في الدنيا , وما يرضيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God may give him a station and honor in the afterlife that satisfies him.
rows.anchor: يعطيك المنزلة في الآخرة , وما يرضيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An orphan is one whose father has died; Muhammad lost both parents when young, was cared for by his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib, then his uncle Abu Talib.
rows.anchor: وسلم فقد أبويه وهو صغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is literal fatherlessness; shelter meant a home and a guardian after the deaths of Abdullah and Abd al-Muttalib.
rows.anchor: من أبويه , فعلى هذا في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: He identifies Abu Talib as the guardian who cared for and supported the Prophet after his father and grandfather died.
rows.anchor: بعد موت عبد الله وعبد المطلب , قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: He says God provided the Prophet a home of his own and made him independent of Abu Talib's care.
rows.anchor: وأغناك عن كفالة أبي طالب , قاله الكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes yatim metaphorically as one of a kind, without equal or counterpart.
rows.anchor: لا مثيل له ولا نظير , من قولهم درة يتيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the metaphorical reading, God sheltered him near Himself and selected him for the Messenger's office.
rows.anchor: فآواك إلى نفسه واختصك برسالته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that God made him a refuge for orphans and caretaker of people after he had been an orphan and dependent.
rows.anchor: بعد أن كنت يتيما , وكفيل الأنام بعد أن كنت مكفولا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He read the verse with a masculine active verb: He found you astray, then you found guidance through Him.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن : ووجدك ضال فهدي , أي وجدك الضال

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: He interprets ʿāʾilan as having dependents, so God provided sufficiency.
rows.anchor: وجدك ذا عيال فكفاك , قاله الأخفش

rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: His line uses ʿāʾil for a needy traveler or poor person.
rows.anchor: لابن السبيل وللفقير العائل

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He interprets the phrase as finding Muhammad poor and making him wealthy.
rows.anchor: الثاني : فقيرا فيسر لك ، قاله الفراء

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The poem uses yaʿīl to mean becoming poor.
rows.anchor: يدري الغني متى يعيل أي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is that he lacked proofs and God enriched him with them.
rows.anchor: أي وجدك فقيرا من الحجج والبراهين , فأغناك بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading says God enriched a poor person through the Prophet; a report has the Prophet repeat that his Lord favors him and is worthy of favor.
rows.anchor: روي أن النبي صلى الله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He interprets taqhar as despising the orphan.
rows.anchor: فلا تحقر , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: He interprets it as not wronging the orphan.
rows.anchor: فلا تظلم , رواه سفيان

rows.speaker: ابن سلام
rows.claim: He interprets it as not humiliating the orphan.
rows.anchor: فلا تستذل , حكاه ابن سلام

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He says not to withhold the orphan's right that is in one's possession.
rows.anchor: فلا تمنعه حقه الذي في يدك , قاله الفراء

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He says to treat an orphan like a merciful father.
rows.anchor: كن لليتيم كالأب الرحيم , وهي في قراءة ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: He read the command with takhar instead of taqhar; al-Hajjaj says kahar means to rebuke or scold.
rows.anchor: وهي في قراءة ابن مسعود : فلا تكهر , قاله أبو الحجاج

rows.speaker: أبو عمران الجوني عن أبي هريرة
rows.claim: They report that the Prophet advised a man with a hard heart to stroke an orphan's head and feed a poor person to soften it.
rows.anchor: أبو عمران الجوني عن أبي هريرة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He says to refuse a beggar gently and kindly if refusing is necessary.
rows.anchor: ورده برحمة ولين , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: He says a religious questioner should not be treated harshly, but answered gently.
rows.anchor: وأجبه برفق ولين , قاله سفيان

rows.speaker: ابن شجرة
rows.claim: He identifies the Lord's favor as prophethood, and the command as inviting one's people.
rows.anchor: النبوة , قاله ابن شجرة , ويكون تأويل قوله فحدث

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He identifies the favor as the Quran, so the command is to convey it to the community.
rows.anchor: أنه القرآن , قاله مجاهد , ويكون قوله : فحدث

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He says the favor includes whatever good or harm one experiences; one may speak of it to trusted brothers or remember it inwardly as gratitude.
rows.anchor: ما أصاب من خير أو شر , قاله الحسن . ( فحدث )

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: He says after completing the obligatory prayers, devote yourself to standing in night prayer.
rows.anchor: من الفرائض فانصب من قيام الليل , قاله ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: He says after finishing prayer, devote yourself to supplication.
rows.anchor: من صلاتك فانصب في دعائك , قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: They say after finishing jihad against the enemy, devote yourself to worship of your Lord.
rows.anchor: من جهادك عدوك فانصب لعبادة ربك , قاله الحسن وقتادة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He says after completing worldly affairs, devote yourself to work for the afterlife.
rows.anchor: من أمر دنياك فانصب في عمل آخرتك , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that after delivering the message, devote yourself to fighting the enemy.
rows.anchor: فرغت من إبلاغ الرسالة فانصب

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: He says to direct one's desire to God in supplication.
rows.anchor: في دعائك قاله ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another meaning is to seek His assistance.
rows.anchor: في معونتك

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He says to direct oneself to God with sincerity of intention.
rows.anchor: في إخلاص نيتك , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is to seek God's help in victory over enemies.
rows.anchor: فارغب إليه في نصرك على

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: One interpretation of the preceding phrase says the reward is uncounted.
rows.anchor: الثاني : غير محسوب , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Another interpretation says the reward is not spoiled by reproach or injury.
rows.anchor: الثالث : غير مكدر بالمن والأذى , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: ابن عيسى
rows.claim: Another interpretation says the reward is not cut off.
rows.anchor: الرابع : غير مقطوع , قاله ابن عيسى

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Another interpretation says it is reward without prior work.
rows.anchor: الخامس : أجر بغير عمل , قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that someone who reaches old age is credited with the reward for good deeds he can no longer perform.
rows.anchor: الهرم كتب له أجر ما

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: He says whatever one does in old age does not harm him.
rows.anchor: أن لا يضر كل أحد منهم ما عمله في كبره , قاله ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He interprets al-din as God's judgment.
rows.anchor: حكم الله تعالى , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another meaning of al-din is requital, supported by the cited verse about the former generations being repaid.
rows.anchor: دنا تميما كما كانت أوائلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question affirms God's supreme judgment to anyone who acknowledges an eternal Creator.
rows.anchor: تقرير لمن اعترف من الكفار

rows.speaker: ابن عيسى
rows.claim: He interprets God as the wisest of judges in craft and governance.
rows.anchor: بأحكم الحاكمين صنعا وتدبيرا , قاله ابن عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that He is the most just in judging truthfully among creatures; an implied question asks why they deny resurrection and requital.
rows.anchor: الخلق وفيه مضمر محذوف , وتقديره : فلم ينكرون

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: He answered the verse with an affirmation that he is among its witnesses, a response the author chooses.
rows.anchor: وكان علي رضي الله عنه
